context:
Goal: a session stays in its own tier: the coordinator plans and briefs, lanes build, triage asks you questions, the batch runner merges. You asked for "an actual fix", a check, not more written rules (Oct 31 15:31 CDT).
Problem (rule): the lane building that check (tier-boundaries-enforced, PR #919) needs to know how hard it stops a session that steps outside its tier. Your rule lets the coordinator make a tiny fix itself when it cannot change any check's result, and a check cannot judge that, so any hard stop also blocks those tiny fixes.
Based on (notes): what happened Oct 31: the coordinator took owner questions that were triage's, ran its own build and review agents, and merged in other repos.
Based on (read): decision session-tiers says no hard block applies to tiers today.
Departs from: session-tiers (no hard block) — a: the check refuses, and your typed override lets one act through.

What the check would stop, in plain terms: the coordinator editing code or guard files instead of sending a lane; the coordinator putting a question on your page instead of triage; a session other than the batch runner merging; the coordinator writing into another repo. Each option says what happens when a session tries one of these.

Meanwhile: PR #919 is built with a (refuse, with your override) and waits for this answer and item 111 before it merges.
holds: PR #919, the tier check, waits for this answer before it merges.

lastAnswer.note: i want to also keep logging to see how this is working

options.gain: The coordinator cannot drift, which is the fix you asked for.
options.how: The check refuses the act and names the right tier. You type override to let one act through.
options.label: Refuse, with your typed override
options.lose: A tiny fix by the coordinator needs your override or a lane.

options.gain: No hard stop; you decide each case.
options.how: The check stops and asks you before the act.
options.label: Ask you each time
options.lose: More prompts to you, and you may not be there to answer.

options.how: The check writes the act to a log and lets it run.
options.label: Log only
options.lose: The same as today: drift goes on.

reply: Filed on step tier-boundaries-enforced (roadmap 4e711fe9): the check refuses, your override lets one act through, and every refusal and override is logged for you to read. The item closes when the lane takes it.
title: How hard does the guard stop a session working outside its tier?
why: Only a refusal stops the drift you saw on Oct 31; your override keeps the rare exception open.
